name: Geographx 4 m natural-colour land-cover basemaps (2012)
description: Commercial 4 m national land-cover raster tiles designed by Geographx using Topo50, LCDB3 and relief from its 8 m DEM.
story: By the September 2012 Taurewa Mountain Cartography Workshop, Geographx had completed a New Zealand-wide set of natural-colour land-cover basemap textures with 4 m pixels. Roger Smith described 116 tiles, each 16,384 pixels square and covering about 65.5 km on a side. The layered Photoshop source files together totalled roughly 420 GB, more than 31 billion pixels.

Unlike a satellite mosaic, the basemap was built from mapped feature data: LINZ Topo50 vectors, land-cover classes substituted from Landcare Research LCDB3, and hillshading from the separately created Geographx 8 m digital elevation model. Smith described Manifold System for GIS preparation, Global Mapper for hillshades and masks, and Adobe Photoshop for scripted layering, tones and textures.

The processing sequence combined physical surfaces, vegetation, built areas, water, transport networks and hillshading. Smith described a script-controlled snowfall effect and exporting registered tiles as GeoTIFF, ECW or PNG for clients. Examples in his 2012 paper show Auckland-area tiles and Skyline TerraExplorer visualisations of the Waitaki and Clarence river landscapes.

The 2015 ICA national report states the 4 m basemap was offered commercially. Its rights differ from the open-licensed 8 m elevation model and from the separate 2013 LINZ TileMill basemap source release. The original 2012 paper has authoritative photographs of Geographx's own screens, but a separate right to republish the paper figures has not been established. A suggested TV3 weather customer remains unverified.
